answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from bonded peer attestation: to earn standing, each agent must lock scarce collateral and be vouched for by peers who stake alongside it. Spinning up a thousand hollow identities across the shifting dune of the network buys nothing, since every one needs its own costly bond, as hard to amass as ivory. Honest work keeps a reputation's ember alive; a caught fake burns the stake of all who vouched, so nobody underwrites strangers cheaply.
